evidence_inventory.observation: D3 ran 2026-10-10T09:56:07.7667636Z to 09:56:47.0988505Z; process_exit_code=1; output absent; returned_tick_count=null; baseline unchanged; D3 result INCONCLUSIVE_FAIL_CLOSED.
Terminal marker JF02_CONNECT_FAILED after exact D3 cache/runtime/request identity lines; no JF02_SUCCESS, tick count, history failure or strategy-start evidence.

Collector calls client.connect(...), then polls client.isConnected() for a hard 30-second deadline. JF02_CONNECT_FAILED is printed only if the client is still not connected at that deadline. Strategy starts only after this gate.

connect(username,password) documents JFAuthenticationException for authentication error and JFVersionException for blocked version; isConnected means authenticated, authorized and transport connected.

DCClientImpl.connect performs getAuthServers -> authenticate -> TransportClient.connect -> connectToHistoryServer before returning. No thrown connect exception reached the launcher because JF02_CONNECT_FAILED was emitted after connect returned.

DCClientImpl.isConnected returns true only when transportClient exists, transportClient.isOnline()==true, and internal initialized==true. initialized becomes true when account-info initialization completes, then fireConnected() calls ISystemListener.onConnect().
Same SDK 3.6.51 / API 2.13.99 previously achieved authentication PASS and instrument subscription PASS; failure occurred later in historical loading.

No additional JForex/Dukascopy log file was found in the user profile and no Java/Application Error event was found in the D3 time window. Raw provider diagnostics therefore cannot distinguish transport-online from initialized=false.

Windows user proxy disabled; no HTTP/HTTPS proxy environment variables present; no Java/JForex application-specific firewall filter found. Firewall profiles are enabled with no explicit Java/JForex app rule observed.
Fresh D3 cache initialized only lock/version metadata; no USATECH exact-hour history cache object was created. Baseline cache remained unchanged.

Official example treats connect/disconnect through ISystemListener.onConnect/onDisconnect and uses repeated connection-state handling rather than defining a provider-level 30-second connection-failure threshold.

timeline.event: client.connect(...) returned without propagating JFAuthenticationException/JFVersionException/other exception to main; exact return timestamp not instrumented.
Collector's fixed connection deadline expires with client.isConnected()==false.
Run finishes after JF02_CONNECT_FAILED; no strategy/getTicks/output.

call_path_analysis.collector: ClientFactory.getDefaultInstance -> setCacheDirectory -> client.connect -> poll isConnected up to 30s -> only then startStrategy
call_path_analysis.sdk_connected_predicate: transportClient != null AND transportClient.isOnline() AND initialized
call_path_analysis.initialization_completion: account-info processing sets initialized=true and fireConnected invokes ISystemListener.onConnect
call_path_analysis.diagnostic_gap: D3 ISystemListener callbacks were empty and the launcher preserved only lines beginning JF02_/BLOCKED_D3_, so no transport-vs-initialization state distinction was retained.

candidate_matrix.basis: For this attempt, connect returned normally and the collector reached its post-connect polling loop. Explicit authentication rejection is documented to throw JFAuthenticationException.
Initial JNLP/auth bootstrap necessarily progressed far enough for connect to return without exception; later service endpoint reachability is not observable.
Later transport path could have failed or stalled, but no exception/log survived to identify DNS/TCP/TLS/HTTP as the cause.
Consistent with a one-off failure, but no provider diagnostic proves it.
connect returned, while isConnected remained false; static implementation shows full readiness additionally requires transport online plus initialized=true.
Same Java/JForex stack previously authenticated and subscribed successfully; no Java/Application Error event observed.
No JFVersionException was propagated and SDK/API stack previously connected successfully.
No active user proxy, proxy environment variables, or Java/JForex app-specific firewall rule was observed; broader network interference cannot be excluded.
The terminal failure is collector-defined at 30s, not a provider-defined failure state. No evidence shows whether readiness would have occurred after the cutoff.
Fresh cache initialization produced normal lock/version metadata and no historical object; no evidence links it to connection non-readiness.
The collector collapses transport-online and initialized state into one isConnected boolean, uses empty system-listener callbacks, and emits only JF02_CONNECT_FAILED, preventing cause discrimination.
Cannot be excluded in absence of provider diagnostic logs.

most_supported_explanation.explanation: The JForex client completed the synchronous bootstrap/authentication portion without an explicit exception but did not reach the SDK's full connected predicate (transport online + session initialized) before the collector's 30-second deadline. Existing evidence cannot distinguish delayed initialization from a later transport/provider failure.

necessity_assessment.reason: A connection-only observability experiment is required to distinguish authentication/version exceptions, transport state, initialization completion and deadline effects before returning to any getTicks causal test.

minimum_next_experiment.title: CONNECTION-ONLY STATE-OBSERVABILITY CONTROL V0.1
constraints: One DEMO login and one connect attempt only; zero reconnect/retry.
No strategy start, no getTicks, no historical request, no market-data acquisition.
Record connect() call duration and exact exception class if thrown.
Observe isConnected at bounded intervals for a preregistered longer window (recommended 120 seconds) without reconnecting.
Use a separately authorized fresh isolated cache; do not touch baseline or D3 cache.
